title: Bidirectional BFS in Reykjavik: Faster Meets!
description: Watch how Bidirectional BFS searches from both start and goal on a street-map graph, meeting in the middle for speed. The visualization shows layered frontiers expanding until the optimal path emerges.
ig_caption:
🌍 Reykjavik (Vesturbær) streets, but make it algorithm magic. ⚡

Bidirectional BFS is a graph search that runs two BFS processes simultaneously: one from the start node and one from the goal node. 🧭 Each side explores outward in increasing distance layers, so the search “meets in the middle,” dramatically reducing explored nodes compared to a single-source BFS on large unweighted road graphs.

In graph-theory terms, your street network becomes an unweighted graph where intersections are vertices and road segments are edges. Bidirectional BFS leverages this structure to find the shortest path by ensuring both frontiers expand level-by-level until a common vertex connects them—then the path is reconstructed by chaining predecessors from both directions. 🧩🚦

When the two searches meet, we stitch the partial paths into a complete route—fewer explored intersections, faster results.
